verdict.rationale: ByteAsk's own `exec` subcommand runs a task headlessly to completion for scripting and CI. It emits JSON Lines and schema-conformant output, and `--sandbox workspace-write` lets it build and test without a human in the loop. /agents and `byteask queue` show sessions working while you are elsewhere. These are one-off runs, though: any recurring schedule or trigger has to come from an external CI system, which earns no credit. missing for 10: a native recurring schedule or event triggers for automations, documented background or daemon automation management, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: For scripting and CI pipelines, use the `exec` subcommand
`byteask exec` - it runs one task to completion and exits.
Use it when a pipeline needs to consume the run rather than a human reading it.
/agents opens a command center grouping your agent sessions into needs-input, working, ready and finished.
